First release of RequestLab, an HTTP inspection and debugging toolkit for the
command line.

RequestLab performs one request at a time and reports what happened: status,
headers, redirect chain, bytes received, response digest, peer address, TLS
certificate details and the timings it can actually measure. It has no runtime
dependencies, verifies certificates with no bypass, and keeps no record of a
request unless asked.

## Included

- `send` and `inspect` for request execution and response inspection, with
  GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD and OPTIONS, custom headers, query
  parameters, and bodies from text, JSON, a file or standard input.
- `compare` for differences in status, headers, size, body digest, final URL
  and redirect count, ignoring volatile headers by default. Timing is reported
  but never counted as a difference.
- `history` and `config`: an opt-in local history that redacts credentials
  before writing and stores no bodies, and stored settings written with mode
  `0600`.
- JSON output on every command behind `--json`, with an envelope versioned
  independently of the tool.
- Optional destination restrictions covering loopback, private, link-local,
  unique-local, multicast, reserved and cloud-metadata addresses, enforced on
  resolved addresses at the connection boundary and repeated on every
  redirect.

## Install

Requires Node.js 20.19 or later. Verify the checksum before extracting:

```sh
base=https://github.com/sablectl/requestlab/releases/download/v1.0.0
curl -fsSLO "$base/requestlab-v1.0.0.tar.gz"
curl -fsSLO "$base/requestlab-v1.0.0.tar.gz.sha256"
sha256sum -c requestlab-v1.0.0.tar.gz.sha256
tar -xzf requestlab-v1.0.0.tar.gz
node requestlab-v1.0.0/dist/bin/requestlab.js --version
```

A checksum proves integrity, not provenance: it defends against a corrupted or
substituted download, not against a compromised release.

This package is not published to npm. GitHub releases are the distribution
channel.

## Known limitations

HTTP/1.1 only, no proxy support, no cookie jar, no compression negotiation,
and no separate DNS, TCP or TLS handshake timings. macOS and Windows are
expected to work but are not tested. The full list is in the README and
`docs/technical-debt.md`.
